title: Amplified guitar and changing styles
summary: He accepts amplified guitar, dislikes bebop, likes rock and roll, and recalls guitarists with Louis Armstrong's band not using amplifiers in the late 1930s.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: How's this business of amplifying a guitar coming in?

Well, I know that some people don't like the amp-fire guitar. And you know who that person is, I ain't called no name. They don't like it. Say they want to hear the guitar playing without the amp-fire. Well, nowadays, I mean, it don't go like that. It's modern times, you know. Everything's changed, you know, the whole world changed. Change in building and overpass, underpass, everything is changed. It's different world today, you know. Same as the music change, I mean. You have progressive. You have bebop. Well, bebop is not so hard, but progressive. It's pretty good music, I think. Bebop, well, I never could stand bebop. Rock and roll, I like. Jazz, well, you know, that's it. I like a lot of commercial tunes, too, with pop tunes, you know. I like to play them, I love to play them. But this particular person don't like an amp-fire. Someday you'll find out who that person is, what I've been telling you. You both know the place, Poison. I don't call no name.
Well, when did they start using amplified guitars around here?
When they started that? Uh-huh. I see. Before the war?
World War II or after? Or during?
I see, you were away with Lily until 39 when you were.

Yeah, 39. Didn't use no amplifier. No. You know the boy in the band, Lee Blatt, didn't use it, no. Will Johnson didn't use it either. Well, Will Johnson played more of the banjo than he did the guitar, because he had a small guitar. I think it was a four-string guitar, I think he had. You recall that?
I never saw Bill Johnson in my life. You never saw Bill Johnson? I'm talking about that guy used to be with Louis Ruffalo. I never saw him.
He passed in Kentucky, didn't he? At his hometown. I don't know. Well, Lee Blatt, he played the guitar, but he didn't have no amplifier, I'm sure that.
But when you came back here from leaving Louis?
Well, then I found that amplifier, yeah.
They had him here in the 30s.
Yeah, they had him here, yeah. Yeah, that's right. That's right.
Did you hear him anywhere on the road with Louis?

No, I don't know. I can't recall. I read him on the road with no place, no. Because I think Lee Blatt would have had one if that would have happened at that particular time. Yeah, I mean, 39 or 37, 38, around that time. They'd have been out, he would have had one, I think. Yeah.
